facility_roles.quote: It was constructed to study high-energy muon and neutrino fluxes and search for new types of ... particles: magnetic monopoles, WIMPs - massive particles which can be considered as candidates to "dark" matter, and others.

intervals.label: first cluster deployed
intervals.note: Named 'Dubna'; the status paper independently confirms the first cluster's deployment year as 2016 (see next interval), so 2015-2016 is recorded as the transition; the earlier 2015 date is the press account's.
intervals.quote: 22 July 2015 ... In early April, members of the Baikal collaboration deployed and started operation of the first cluster of the Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD). Named “Dubna”, the cluster comprises 192 optical modules

intervals.label: expanding cluster array (ongoing)
intervals.note: As of the winter 2023 campaign: 3456 OMs on 96 strings (per the same source). The array is explicitly still being expanded toward its planned cubic-kilometre scale.
intervals.quote: The first cluster of the Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope was deployed in 2016 with 288 OMs. Since then, there has been an annual increase of the deployed clusters.

intervals.label: deployed clusters taking physics data (ongoing)
intervals.note: Verification fix (2026-09-17): added because the growing array has been taking physics data continuously since 2018 (astrophysical-neutrino searches published using 2018-2021/2018-2022 data) while construction continues, the same overlapping construction/commissioning pattern recorded for experiment:km3net. Corrects an omission where only a bare 'construction' status was recorded despite sourced evidence of ongoing data-taking.
intervals.quote: The Baikal-GVD data collected in 2018-2022 indicate the presence of cosmic neutrino flux in high-energy cascade events consistent with observations by the IceCube neutrino telescope.

physics_goals.quote: It was constructed to study high-energy muon and neutrino fluxes and search for new types of ... particles: magnetic monopoles, WIMPs - massive particles which can be considered as candidates to "dark" matter, and others.
physics_goals.value: Detect high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and search for new types of elementary particles using a large-volume underwater Cherenkov array

summary.plain: A growing underwater telescope in Lake Baikal, Siberia, that has been adding new clusters of light sensors every year since 2016 in search of neutrinos from deep space.
summary.technical: Expanding underwater Cherenkov neutrino telescope in Lake Baikal's southern basin; first Baikal-GVD cluster deployed 2016, growing to 3456 OMs on 96 strings by the winter 2023 deployment campaign; already-deployed clusters have taken continuous physics data since 2018 (published astrophysical-neutrino searches using 2018-2022 data) while construction toward a design cubic-kilometre-scale volume continues.
